title: When too much turns bitter
literal_meaning: If you squeeze a lemon too much, it turns bitter.
english_summary: Pressing a useful action too far can spoil its result; the warning is about proportion, not effort itself.
explanation: The useful action—extracting juice—becomes counterproductive when carried too far. The warning is about proportion: pressing for one more favour, one more concession or one more advantage may damage what was already achieved. It does not mean that effort itself is bad.

literal_meaning: You will keep washing the sack and singing praises.
english_summary: The trouble continues, and so does the rueful memory of who brought it about.
explanation: The praise has an ironic edge. The source explains the expression as remembering someone after receiving a hard lesson from them. literal_meaning: According to the stake, the horse leaps.

explanation: The source applies this image to disorder under weak supervision. The horse’s movement is viewed in relation to what holds it, so the remark turns attention from the actor alone to the arrangement around them. That wider application is editorial; the source does not supply a history of the image.
